evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/facilities/pages/PendingBookingsPage.tsx — the manager-facing approve/reject actions swallow API failures with no user-facing feedback. handleApprove (L54-63) and handleRejectConfirm (L74-89) wrap approveBooking/rejectBooking in try/catch whose only failure handling is `console.error(...)`; on error the in-try `refreshBookings()` is skipped so the list is not even reloaded. A manager who clicks Approve on a booking that fails server-side sees the row unchanged and NO error — indistinguishable from a slow success — and may believe the booking was approved when it was not.

Same file, refreshBookings (L30-44): a failed listPendingBookings is caught to console.error only, then isLoading is set false with bookings left as the previous/empty array. On the initial load path this renders the BookingList empty-state, so a fetch error is shown to the manager as 'no pending bookings' — actively hiding pending approvals. Identical masking in features/facilities/pages/FacilitiesPage.tsx (fetchFacilities L58-72: catch → console.error only → empty FacilityList) and features/facilities/pages/MyBookingsPage.tsx (fetch L38-39 and cancel L75-76: catch → console.error only).

Confirmed no error surface exists in the whole feature: grep for setError|toast|ErrorBanner|<Alert|errorMessage across PendingBookingsPage.tsx, MyBookingsPage.tsx, FacilitiesPage.tsx returns nothing. The codebase already has the correct pattern to copy — features/emergency/pages/EmergencyContactDirectoryPage.tsx handleCreate/handleUpdate (L97-133) set an error state AND use i18n: `setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : t('emergency.errors.failedToCreate'))`. Fix: give the facilities pages the same error state (surface a banner/toast on load + action failure, and do not render the empty-state when the last load errored), reusing t('...') keys. Confidence medium: reachability is certain; whether the backend can realistically 4xx these calls in normal use was not runtime-confirmed.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/portfolio-performance/pages/PortfolioListPage.tsx:11-49 ships a shipped, route-mounted page that renders a HARDCODED `mockPortfolios` constant instead of real data. The comment on L10 says '// Mock data - would be fetched from API'. The page imports only React, useState, and PortfolioCard (L2-4) — there is no API client, no useQuery, no loading/error state — so every manager who opens the Portfolio list is shown three fabricated portfolios with fake financials (e.g. 'Core Investment Portfolio' €2,500,000 value / €1,200,000 equity / 4 properties, L14-23).

The fake data drives real UI math: the summary tiles are computed from the mock via `mockPortfolios.filter(p => p.isActive).reduce(...)` (L60-71, totalValue/totalEquity/propertyCount) and the show-inactive toggle filters the mock (L57-58). Nothing here degrades gracefully to real data — the API wiring simply does not exist, so this is fabricated business data presented as genuine, not a stub placeholder.

Distinct from the existing (dropped) `dx-portfolio-dashboard-stubs` signal, which concerns PortfolioDashboardPage.tsx no-op alert mutations + navigation TODOs — a different file and different concern. Fix: replace mockPortfolios with the real portfolios list query (mirror the useQuery + loading/empty/error pattern used elsewhere in the feature) and delete the constant. Confidence medium: the mock rendering is certain from static read; whether a backing portfolios list endpoint/client already exists was not fully traced.
